_README: High/critical advisories in the PRODUCTION dependency tree that CI is allowed to pass with.
Read by scripts/audit-gate.mjs. Anything not listed here fails CI.
Every entry needs a 'reason' (why it is safe to ship today, specific to this app — not 'low risk')
and an 'expires' date. Past its expiry the entry stops working and CI fails, which is the point:
an accepted risk has to be re-argued on a schedule instead of quietly becoming permanent.
To re-check an entry:  npm audit --omit=dev
To re-check the gate:  npm run audit:gate

advisories.reason: Unauthenticated RCE on Windows-hosted Next.js servers only. This app is deployed on Ubuntu 24.04 (docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) and has no Windows target, so the vulnerable code path is unreachable. Fixed only in next@16; see the tracking note below.

Unauthenticated RCE in the Image Optimization API via AVIF input. This app never imports next/image and sets no images.remotePatterns/domains, so /_next/image will not fetch attacker-supplied remote images, and the app has no file-upload surface to plant a local one. Mitigated by configuration, NOT patched. Fixed only in next@16.
SSRF in applications using WebSocket upgrades. This app opens no WebSocket and has no upgrade handler (verified: no 'websocket'/'socket.io' reference in src/). Vulnerable path unreachable.
Middleware/proxy bypass in Pages Router applications using i18n. This app is App Router only (no pages/ directory) and configures no i18n. Vulnerable path unreachable.

DoS in App Router via Server Actions. This app defines no Server Actions (verified: no 'use server' directive anywhere in src/) — all mutations go through /api route handlers. Vulnerable path unreachable. NOTE: next.config.mjs still narrows serverActions.allowedOrigins defensively; if a Server Action is ever added, this entry must be re-assessed.
SSRF in Server Actions on custom servers. This app defines no Server Actions and runs under plain `next start` behind nginx, not a custom Node server. Vulnerable path unreachable.
SSRF in rewrites via an attacker-controlled destination hostname. next.config.mjs defines no rewrites() and no redirects(). Vulnerable path unreachable.

ACCEPTED RESIDUAL RISK, not unreachable: DoS via HTTP request deserialization in React Server Components, which this App Router app does use. Impact is availability only — no data disclosure and no code execution. Partially mitigated by nginx in front and by per-IP rate limiting (server/http/rateLimit.ts). Accepted at single-facility pilot scale; must be resolved by the next@16 upgrade.
ACCEPTED RESIDUAL RISK: DoS with Server Components. Same reasoning, mitigation and upgrade path as GHSA-h25m-26qc-wcjf.
ACCEPTED RESIDUAL RISK: DoS with Server Components. Same reasoning, mitigation and upgrade path as GHSA-h25m-26qc-wcjf.

Arbitrary file read via attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL in CSS. postcss here is a build-time-only transitive dependency of next/tailwind, processing only first-party CSS committed to this repo — there is no path by which untrusted CSS reaches it. Not reachable at runtime. Pinned by next@14's bundled copy; fixed only in next@16.
Same build-time-only postcss source-map path traversal as GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q; same reasoning and same next@16 fix.

_TRACKING: Almost every entry above shares one root cause: next is pinned to 14.2.35, which is the FINAL 14.x
release. There will be no further 14.x security patches — npm reports the only fix as next@16.3.8,
a two-major upgrade. Every entry here expires 2026-12-31 to force that upgrade to be scheduled
rather than deferred indefinitely. See docs/SCALING_PLAN.md 'Known gaps'.
